title: Las Vegas to Phoenix, Arizona
dek: Six days and 1,615 miles between Christmas and New Year: the Mojave and Joshua Tree, Route 66 to Kingman, Sedona’s red rock, the Salt River Canyon and the Mogollon Rim, ending in the Valley of the Sun.

days.label: Day 1
prose: Breakfast at Primm & Proper inside the Primm Valley Resort & Casino. The avocado toast, with poached egg, tomatoes and wild greens on country-grilled bread, is hard to beat.

No trip through the Mojave is complete without Roy’s Motel & Cafe in Amboy. The 1940s diner no longer serves hot food, but there’s Route 66 Root Beer and snacks to hold you until Joshua Tree. The pumps work, at some of the highest gas prices on Route 66.
At the gateway to Joshua Tree National Park, the Joshua Tree Saloon does food, beer on tap and live music.
highlights: Hike Hidden Valley, an easy one-mile loop among the rock walls, with succulents and wildflowers in late winter and spring.
Keys View, over 5,000 feet up, looks across the Coachella Valley to Palm Springs, Indio and the San Andreas Fault, and on a clear day to Signal Mountain in Mexico.

lodging.name: Best Western Plus A Wayfarer’s Inn, Kingman

days.label: Day 4
road: Desert mountains and Canyon Lake. Route 88 leads to Tortilla Flat; it was repaved in recent years, a huge improvement. Many turn back there, but the next 8 miles of good pavement are worth riding, and adventure bikes can carry on along the packed gravel toward Roosevelt for high canyon walls.

lodging.name: Best Western Copper Hills Inn, Globe

days.label: Day 5
road: One of the best lesser-known rides in Arizona: down through the Salt River Canyon on a varied mix of turns, with hairpins near the river and good pull-offs for the views. There are few towns or gas stations, so fuel up when you can.

days.label: Day 6
road: South from Flagstaff’s forests into Sedona, turn after turn, with cliff overlooks and red-rock views. Many riders say southbound is the direction to ride it. Then the Beeline Highway, AZ-87, down to the Valley.
